name: Kinesiology Major

sections.title: Program Requirements

requirements.title: Students complete 120 units, as specified below

sections.title: Lower Division Requirements
sections.note:
The program’s lower division requirements are structured as a common core set, an additional set of courses for the kinesiology general program, or the optional active health and rehabilitation concentration, and general elective courses that include the university's breadth requirements.
Students complete all of the following.

requirements.title: One of PHYS 101, PHYS 120, PHYS 125, PHYS 140
One of PHYS 102, PHYS 121, PHYS 126, PHYS 141
One of BPK 110, BPK 180W, BPK 241
requirements.note: Students who choose the kinesiology general program will complete one of.

sections.title: Active Health and Rehabilitation Concentration
sections.note: Students who choose this concentration will complete all of.

sections.title: Breadth and Writing Requirements

requirements.title: Check with an advisor
requirements.text: For students admitted prior to September 2006, a minimum of six units must be selected from the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences.

requirements.title: Check with an advisor
requirements.text: For students admitted September 2006 or later, a minimum of six units of designated humanities breadth (B-Hum) courses, and a minimum of six units of designated social sciences breadth (B-Soc) courses must be completed.

requirements.title: Check with an advisor
requirements.text: At least three units of lower division course work should also be identified as writing-intensive (W) courses.

sections.note:
The quantitative (Q), science breadth (B-Sci) and undesignated breadth (UB) requirements are satisfied through completion of the Kinesiology lower division core course set and hence do not require additional work.
For more information, see www.sfu.ca/ugcr .

requirements.text: Students complete either the general program requirements as listed immediately below, or they can choose to complete the requirements for the active health and rehabilitation concentration (see below).

sections.title: General Program

requirements.title: Check with an advisor
requirements.text: This program option requires a total of at least 45 upper division units, which is composed of the upper division core courses as shown above and the following additional requirements.

requirements.title: Check with an advisor
requirements.text: Students who choose this option will complete an additional 21 biomedical physiology and kinesiology units chosen from upper division BPK courses, excluding BPK 325, 342, 457, 459, 491, 495 and 499.

requirements.title: Check with an advisor
requirements.text: A minimum of three of these 21 units must be from 400 level BPK courses.

requirements.title: Check with an advisor
requirements.text: Students admitted in September 2006 or later are also required to complete the university's writing, quantitative and breadth (WQB) requirements, which includes the requirement of completing three units of writing-intensive credit at the upper division.

sections.note:
MBB 321 may be used to satisfy three units of this requirement.
As well, an additional three upper division units, chosen from any department within the university including BPK, but excluding BPK 325, 342, 457, 459, 491,495 and 499.
The W component may be included within the 45 upper division unit total for this general program.

sections.title: Professional School Transfer

requirements.title: Check with an advisor
requirements.text: Students are eligible to receive a bachelor of science (BSc) degree after the completion of their second year of professional study if they have completed at least 90 units of Simon Fraser University credit normally comprising the following: all lower division requirements the upper division core requirements for their major acceptance into an accredited professional program in dentistry, medicine, optometry, chiropractic, or veterinary medicine.

requirements.title: Check with an advisor
requirements.text: Professional program courses must not duplicate those already completed at Simon Fraser University and must be acceptable for transfer credit to the university.

sections.note: Candidates apply for transfer credit and for receipt of the degree through Student Services.

sections.title: Other requirements
sections.note:
NOTE: SFU students accepted in the accelerated master's within the Department of Biomedical Physiology and Kinesiology may apply a maximum of nine BPK graduate course units, taken while completing the bachelor's degree, towards the upper division electives of the bachelor's program and the requirements of the master's degree.
For more information go to: https://www.sfu.ca/gradstudies/apply/programs/accelerated-masters.html .

sections.title: Elective Courses
sections.note: In addition to the courses listed above, students should consult an academic advisor to plan the remaining required elective courses.

grades.label: Continuance Requirement
grades.text: After a student has completed 24 credits, a Science cumulative grade point average (CGPA) of not less than 2.50 is required for continuance in the major.

grades.label: Continuance Requirement
grades.text: Students, whose Science CGPA falls below 2.50, will be sent a warning letter and if at the end of the subsequent term the Science CGPA is less than 2.50, these students shall be withdrawn from the BIF or KIN Major.

grades.label: Continuance Requirement
grades.text: Students who have completed 90 or more units and whose Science CGPA falls below a 2.50, but is at least 2.00, will be allowed to complete their Biomedical Physiology or Kinesiology major.
